# INNOVA AirLeaf ECA644II (deviceType 002) + Shelly Gen3

> Tested community integration for local monitoring and control of an INNOVA AirLeaf ECA644II fan-coil controller that reports `deviceType` `002`, using a Shelly Gen3 script, Shelly Virtual Components and the unit's local HTTP API.

## Canonical project

- Repository: https://github.com/drHouse-gif/drHouse-gif-innova-airleaf-shelly
- Human documentation: `README.md`
- Machine-oriented context: `AI_CONTEXT.md`
- Structured metadata: `project.yaml`
- Production controller: `innova-airleaf-controller.js`
- Architecture: `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Upstream submission notes: `docs/UPSTREAM_SUBMISSION.md`

## Hardware requirements

- Target HVAC device: INNOVA AirLeaf ECA644II.
- Validated API identity: `deviceType` = `002`.
- Controller host: Shelly Gen3 device with scripting and Shelly Virtual Components support.
- Network: Shelly and INNOVA must have local IPv4 reachability; TCP port 80 must be reachable.
- Recommended addressing: static IP or DHCP reservation for the INNOVA controller.

## Local API

Base URL: `http://INNOVA_IP/api/v/1/`

| Operation | Method | Endpoint | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| Status | GET | `/api/v/1/status` | none |
| Power on | POST | `/api/v/1/power/on` | `{}` |
| Power off | POST | `/api/v/1/power/off` | `{}` |
| Heating mode | POST | `/api/v/1/set/mode/heating` | `{}` |
| Cooling mode | POST | `/api/v/1/set/mode/cooling` | `{}` |
| Set temperature | POST | `/api/v/1/set/setpoint` | `{"temp":220}` for 22.0 °C |
| Fan auto | POST | `/api/v/1/set/function/auto` | `{}` |
| Fan night | POST | `/api/v/1/set/function/night` | `{}` |
| Fan minimum | POST | `/api/v/1/set/function/min` | `{}` |
| Fan maximum | POST | `/api/v/1/set/function/max` | `{}` |

Temperatures are represented by the INNOVA API in tenths of a degree Celsius.

## Status field map

- `ps`: power state; `1` means on.
- `sp`: target temperature in tenths of °C.
- `ta`: measured room temperature in tenths of °C.
- `wm`: working mode; validated values: `3 = heating`, `5 = cooling`.
- `fn`: fan function; validated values: `1 = auto`, `2 = night`, `3 = min`, `4 = max`.

Unknown values must not be guessed or generalized.

## Shelly Virtual Components

The current production script expects six fixed components:

- `boolean:200` — Power — read/write.
- `enum:201` — Mode: `heating`, `cooling` — read/write.
- `number:202` — Set temperature: 16–31 °C, 0.5 °C step — read/write.
- `enum:203` — Fan: `auto`, `night`, `min`, `max` — read/write.
- `number:204` — Room temperature — display/read-only.
- `text:205` — Connection/error status — display/read-only.

## Runtime logic

1. Resolve the six Virtual Component handles.
2. Register handlers for power, mode, setpoint and fan changes.
3. Poll `/status` immediately and then every 15 seconds when the HTTP queue is idle.
4. Serialize requests through a FIFO queue; at most one HTTP request is active.
5. Limit the waiting queue to six requests.
6. Use a 5-second HTTP timeout and independent 8-second watchdog.
7. Reject status synchronization unless the response reports `deviceType` `002`.
8. Validate user values before sending commands; setpoints are normalized to 0.5 °C.
9. After every accepted control command, read physical status again and publish the real device state.
10. Ignore script-originated Virtual Component events to prevent feedback loops.

## Home Assistant

Home Assistant is optional. The integration runs locally on Shelly. Supported Shelly Virtual Components can be exposed through the Home Assistant Shelly integration, but this project does not create a native Home Assistant `climate` entity.

## Safety and scope

- Community project; not an official INNOVA, Shelly Group or Home Assistant integration.
- Protocol behavior was validated for a real installation reporting `deviceType` `002`.
- Do not assume other INNOVA device types use identical endpoints, field values or semantics.
- Communication is plain local HTTP; do not expose the INNOVA API directly to the public internet.
- The script does not require cloud credentials and does not open an inbound internet service.
- Current upstream-readiness limitation: `ALLTERCO/shelly-script-examples` expects runtime Virtual Component scripts to self-create/verify their components; the current production script expects components `200..205` to exist first.
